title: IT Staff Interview: Dmitri Volkov Background

fields.organization: North Coast Regional Airport Authority — IT Department
fields.summary: Interview with three senior IT staff members (including two who worked directly with Dmitri Volkov) confirms that Volkov was a high-performing NexGen Solutions contractor who led the AODB migration project. He had full administrative access to the AODB server and was responsible for creating the service account svc_nexgen_aodb. He was informally promised a full-time IT role after project completion, which was later posted externally. This caused visible behavioral changes in his final two weeks: he became quieter, avoided team gatherings, and spent extended time in the server room after hours. All three staff members noted he never expressed dissatisfaction verbally but became emotionally withdrawn.

findings.notes: Dmitri Volkov had full admin rights on AODB server (10.1.10.20) and PACS system (NCIA-PACS-CORE).
svc_nexgen_aodb account not disabled after off-boarding; remains active and accessible from external network.
Volkov had authority to create and modify scheduled tasks on AODB server.
Volkov accessed server room via badge on 10/20/2026 at 23:47; confirmed by PACS and CCTV.
Volkov had capability to deploy and execute PowerShell scripts on AODB server.
No formal complaint or documentation of dissatisfaction. Emotional withdrawal noted in final two weeks, but no record of threat or intent.
Post-project off-boarding failed to revoke service account and failed to conduct exit interview with contract employee.
All IT staff completed annual cybersecurity training (1.4.1).
Employees trained to report concerns via ncia-secops.ncia-airport.org.
Volkov used active badge to enter server room 27 days ago; badge was deactivated 2 days later but access was not blocked.

actionsTaken: Interviewed three IT staff members on-site
Reviewed access logs for Volkov (d.volkov) and svc_nexgen_aodb
Confirmed service account was not removed during off-boarding
Documented behavioral changes in final two weeks
Notified IT Director and Security Lead via secure chat (09:14)
recommendations: Immediately disable svc_nexgen_aodb account and audit all associated activities
Conduct a root-cause review of contractor off-boarding process
Implement mandatory exit interviews for all contractors
Update SIEM rules to flag any script execution by service accounts
Add behavioral anomaly detection to IT staff monitoring
fields.photosNote: 2 photos attached: IMG_0418-0423 (CCTV still of Volkov entering server room, 11:47 PM, 10/20/2026), IMG_0423-0424 (badge scan log from 10/20/2026, 23:47) — both from NCIA-VIDEO-A (SEC-NVR-01)

instructorNote: This inject confirms motive and access for the logic bomb. The emotional withdrawal is a key behavioral clue. The facilitator should watch for teams dismissing this as 'just a guy who got passed over' rather than recognizing it as a red flag.
